lines.trans: Friends of Jasmine Street, forgive my tired travel voice and let Nour share my thanks.
Read loud and clear so the back tables by the fountain basin hear too, Nour!
Thirty Mays ago, a rainy week trapped a young traveller inside Room Eight.
That was the exact week your aunt poured hot tea and started the sunroom waltz!
Listen: I spent thirty years drawing great cities, yet no place ever felt warmer than here.
Lift away the brown wrapping paper with me on three, Salma—one, two, three!
OH! Look at the walnut frame—it is a giant hand-painted map of Jasmine Street!
There is the stone fountain, the clock tower, the bookshop arch, and the park bench!
And right in the middle, painted in warm gold leaf, sits Jasmine Courtyard House and Room Nine!
Look at the tiny figures he painted in our courtyard—someone even has forehead glasses!
Hey! That distinguished gentleman by the gate is remarkably handsome, thank you very much!

words.gloss: I mean; thank you very much

See you soon!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of أكثر ('more, most').

examples.trans: I liked working here much more.
Who knows the neighbourhood better than you?

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun meaning 'family/parents' or 'people of a place' (يا أهل شارع الياسمين 'friends/folks of Jasmine Street').

examples.trans: Welcome to the friends of Jasmine Street!
My family comes to visit me every Friday.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Name of the month of May in the Levantine calendar.

examples.trans: My birthday is in May.
In May the weather gets nice in Amman.

meanings.note: Standard and Jordanian noun for a picture frame (إطار الجوز 'walnut frame') or tyre. Plural: إطارات.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة جوا إطار جوز حلو.
examples.trans: We placed the map inside a lovely walnut frame.
This wooden frame protects the drawing.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببدا, بيبدا).

examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.
The day began lively and bright.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical tower, a skyscraper, or an astrological sign.

examples.trans: The downtown clock tower is old.
We heard the tower bell at noon.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بنية, plural: بنيين).

examples.trans: The brown leather notebook is on the desk.
A clean pair of men's brown shoes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تحيات.

examples.trans: Here is to all our kind neighbours!
He returned the greeting with a warm smile.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Universal everyday Jordanian adjective for 'tired' (feminine: تعبانة, plural: تعبانين).

examples.text: أنا تعبان شوي من رحلة الباص الطويلة.
examples.trans: I am a little tired from the long bus trip.

examples.text: صوتي تعبان اليوم، بس قلبي فرحان.
examples.trans: My voice is tired today, but my heart is glad.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of غلّف ('to wrap/package'). ورق تغليف means 'wrapping paper'.

examples.text: فكينا ورق التغليف البني عن اللوحة.
examples.trans: We removed the brown wrapping paper from the painting.
Good wrapping keeps cake fresh.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجبنة.

examples.trans: Your glasses are pushed up on your forehead!
He wiped the rain off his forehead.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Form I verb (بحبس / حبس). Used literally for confining or playfully when rain traps someone indoors.

examples.text: أسبوع شتا حبس المسافر بغرفة تمانية.
examples.trans: A rainy week trapped the traveller in Room Eight.

examples.text: المطر حبسنا جوا القاعة طول الصبح.
examples.trans: The rain kept us inside the hall all morning.

meanings.note: Used to mean 'even' (e.g., even he went) or 'until' (e.g., until tomorrow).

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Standard and Jordanian feminine noun for a public park or walled garden (حدائق 'parks').

examples.trans: The park bench is painted beside the arch.

examples.text: بنتمشى بالحديقة كل يوم جمعة العصر.
examples.trans: We walk in the park every Friday afternoon.

meanings.note: Form II causative of حس ('to feel'). حسّسني بدفا means 'made me feel warm'.

examples.text: ولا مكان حسّسني بدفا أكتر من هون.
examples.trans: No place ever made me feel warmer than here.
Your kind words made me feel at ease.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth at night.
Morning warmth from the sun is comforting.

meanings.note: Pronounced dahab in Jordanian Arabic (often spelled دهب in dialectal writing). ورق دهب means 'gold leaf'.

examples.text: بيت الياسمين مرسوم بورق دهب دافي.
examples.trans: Jasmine Courtyard House is painted in warm gold leaf.

examples.text: ساعة الجد فيها إطار ذهب قديم.
examples.trans: Grandfather's watch has an old gold frame.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for drawing a picture, a map or a plan.

examples.trans: He drew me a map to the shop on a piece of paper.

examples.text: بنتي بترسم بيوت وشجر كل يوم.
examples.trans: My daughter draws houses and trees every day.

meanings.note: Standard verb for lifting something up or raising.

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Form III verb (بسامح / سامح). سامحني / سامحوا means 'forgive me / excuse me'.

examples.text: سامحوا صوتي التعبان من السفر الطويل.
examples.trans: Forgive my tired voice from the long trip.

examples.text: سامحني يا معلم، ما كان قصدي.
examples.trans: Forgive me, boss, I did not mean to.

meanings.note: In Amman and Levantine cities, سبيل المي is a public stone drinking fountain.

examples.trans: Wait for me by the stone drinking fountain.

examples.text: سبيل الحارة مبني من حجر أبيض.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood fountain is built of white stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: كتب السفر are travel books; على سفر means 'away travelling'.

examples.trans: I love travelling by bus.
My brother is away travelling this week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمح, بيسمح).

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Allow me to pour the orange juice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for 'gentleman' or formal 'Mr.' (plural: سادة).

examples.text: هادا السيد الوقور جنب البوابة وسيم كتير!
examples.trans: That distinguished gentleman by the gate is very handsome!
Mr. Mazen welcomes guests with a smile.

meanings.note: Used both as a masculine adjective ('young traveller' مسافر شاب) and a noun ('young man'). Feminine: شابة, plural: شباب.

examples.text: أسبوع شتا حبس مسافر شاب هون.
examples.trans: A rainy week trapped a young traveller here.
The young people helped carry the chairs to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, شتا means both the winter season and rain.

examples.trans: Winter water is very cold in the morning.
I love the sound of winter rain on the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أشخاص.

examples.trans: The person left a small note on the door.
The table seats four people.

meanings.note: Traditional Levantine word for an iron hook-and-eye latch on wooden shutters or doors.

examples.text: رفعنا شنكل الحديد ففتح الشيش فورا.
examples.trans: We lifted the iron hook latch and the shutter swung right open.

examples.text: سكر شنكل الشباك منيح قبل ما تنام.
examples.trans: Fasten the window latch securely before going to sleep.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصب, بيصب).

examples.text: صبي المي السخنة بالإبريق يا نور.
examples.trans: Pour the hot water into the pot, Nour.
Allow me to pour the orange juice.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضيع, بيضيع).

examples.text: فكرت القطار ضاع لما بعنا البيت!
examples.trans: I thought the train got lost when we sold the house!
You will not get lost; the road is straight.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Can mean physically high or loud (for a voice or sound).

examples.trans: What is that loud sound upstairs?
The wooden ceiling is high and sunny.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعلق, بيعلق).

examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror?
We hung the lanterns in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Arabic distinguishes father's sister (عمة, feminine of عمّ) from mother's sister (خالة).

examples.text: عمتي كانت تعزف عالبيانو كل يوم جمعة.
examples.trans: My paternal aunt used to play the piano every Friday.

examples.text: هاد الدفتر الأخضر هدية من عمتي.
examples.trans: This green notebook is a gift from my aunt.

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Musical loanword (from French valse) for a triple-time piano or orchestral waltz.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد فالس هادي بغرفة القزاز.
examples.trans: Suad played a gentle waltz in the sunroom.

examples.text: عنوان الورقة القديمة هو فالس الساحة.
examples.trans: The title on the old sheet is Courtyard Waltz.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Literally 'sitting', but widely used as an auxiliary participle to denote continuous present action (like English '-ing').

examples.trans: Who is sitting in our courtyard under the tree?
We are sitting having tea.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Defective verb (بقضي / قضيت) from root ق-ض-ي, meaning to spend hours, days, or a summer.

examples.text: قضوا الساعات اللي بعد الضهر جوا.
examples.trans: They spent the afternoon hours inside.
We spent the whole summer in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقواس.

examples.text: ادخل عالساحة من هاد القوس الحجري.
examples.trans: Step into the courtyard through this stone arch.

examples.text: الأقواس القديمة مبنية من حجر عمان.
examples.trans: The old arches are built of Amman limestone.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Conditional particle used for hypothetical or impossible situations (contrary-to-fact conditions).

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Even if he is a little late, wait for him.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مدن.

examples.trans: Amman is an old, lovely hilltop city.
City law protects public gardens.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مرسومة, plural: مرسومين).

examples.text: في مفتاح دهبي مرسوم فوق الباب.
examples.trans: There is a golden key painted above the door.
The map is drawn by hand.

meanings.note: Form III active participle of سافر ('to travel'), used as a noun for someone on a trip or at a bus station.

examples.trans: I should ask another traveller.
The passengers are standing by the door.

meanings.note: Describes weather or a place receiving plenty of sunlight.

examples.trans: Please sit beside the sunny window.
The sunny attic room overlooks the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مكتبات.

examples.trans: There are old bookshops in downtown Amman.
The public library is a quiet place to read.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for feminine singular objects.

examples.trans: This is my friend Dina.
This idea is excellent.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian distal demonstrative ('that over there / that past...'); feminine هديك (hadiik), plural هدولاك.

examples.text: بتذكر هداك الربيع لما فتحنا النزل؟
examples.trans: Do you remember that spring when we opened the inn?

examples.text: حط الصندوق على هداك الرف العالي.
examples.trans: Put the box on that high shelf.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Colloquial attention-getting exclamation, used playfully among friends or family.

examples.trans: Hey! Tariq drove the bus himself!
Hey, where are you going so fast?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واضحة, plural: واضحين).

examples.trans: A sincere, clear sentence from the heart.
The address is clear on the card.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Classic adjective on the فَعِيل pattern from root و-س-م ('mark of beauty').

examples.trans: The young man in the photo is very handsome.
His clothes were neat and he looked handsome.

meanings.note: Intensive adjective (فَعُول) from وقار ('dignity/calm poise'), describing quiet grace and gravitas.

examples.trans: That young man with the dignified appearance.
The professor is dignified and everyone respects him.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?
